title: MONSTER Alarm Clock
tagline: Build an unhackable bedside desk clock with real-time clock chip, I2C LCD, and snooze buzzer!

phases.instructions: Collect the DS3231 RTC module (with CR2032 coin cell), 1602 I2C LCD display, piezo buzzer, and breadboard jumpers.
verificationCheckpoints: DS3231 RTC module ready with coin cell battery
1602 LCD with black I2C backpack board attached

phases.instructions: Connect both the RTC and LCD to the Arduino I2C bus. Because I2C uses unique hardware addresses, both devices share SDA (A4) and SCL (A5) lines!
verificationCheckpoints: Both SDA pins connected to A4
Both SCL pins connected to A5

phases.instructions: Verify that neither I2C device has crossed lines between SDA and SCL, and verify 5V power rails.
verificationCheckpoints: Power rail 5V connected to Red bus
Ground rail connected to Dark Slate bus
No crossed signal wires between A4 and A5

phases.instructions: Study how the RTClib library queries time registers over I2C and prints formatted HH:MM:SS text to the LiquidCrystal_I2C screen.
phases.codeExplanation:
- Wire.h manages I2C bus communication between Arduino, RTC, and LCD.
- rtc.now() queries battery-backed time from the DS3231 oscillator.
- lcd.print() draws formatted two-digit time strings on row 0.
- When current hour and minute match alarm settings, tone() sounds.
verificationCheckpoints: Understand how 2 devices share 2 I2C wires via unique addresses (0x68 and 0x27)
Understand time comparison logic for alarm trigger

phases.instructions: Upload the alarm clock sketch. Adjust the blue contrast potentiometer on the back of the LCD with a small screwdriver until characters appear crisp and sharp.
verificationCheckpoints: Adjust contrast trimmer so black text is clear against blue backlight

phases.instructions: Congratulations! You mastered multi-device I2C bus arbitration and built a functional real-time clock.
verificationCheckpoints: RTC retains time even when USB unplugged
Ready to claim Time Master badge

story: Build an unhackable desktop alarm clock! You will wire a precision DS3231 real-time clock module with battery backup, an I2C 1602 liquid crystal display, and an alarm buzzer that ensures you never miss morning monster training.

troubleshooting.symptom: LCD shows 16 solid white boxes and no text
troubleshooting.cause: Contrast potentiometer out of adjustment or wrong I2C address
troubleshooting.solution: Turn the blue potentiometer on the back of the LCD module until text appears, or verify whether I2C address is 0x27 or 0x3F.
diagnosticSteps: Turn the brass contrast trimmer screw on the back of the I2C backpack.
Run an I2C scanner sketch to verify if address is 0x27 or 0x3F.

troubleshooting.symptom: Time resets to 2000/01/01 every time USB is unplugged
troubleshooting.cause: DS3231 coin cell battery missing or dead
troubleshooting.solution: Insert a fresh CR2032 3V coin cell battery into the RTC battery holder.
diagnosticSteps: Check CR2032 coin battery orientation (+ side facing up).
Verify battery contacts are clean and tight.
